You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

        info.append((v,rs[0],rs[-1],lcol,gap,min(rs)))
    return info,comps

        if len(rows)>1:

        else:  # horizontal bar
            gaps=[c for c in range(cs[0],cs[-1]+1) if O[rows[0]][c]==0 and c!=rows[0]]
            L=gaps[0] if gaps else cs[0]
            bycol[L].append((v,min(rows),max(rows)))
    for L,items in bycol.items():

        prev=-1
        for v,st,br in items:

            prev=max(prev,br)

import collections,json
def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    O=[row[:] for row in I]
    # 1) fill single-cell gaps flanked by equal nonzero colors
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if O[r][c]==0 and c>0 and c<W-1 and O[r][c-1]!=0 and O[r][c+1]!=0 and O[r][c-1]==O[r][c+1]:
                O[r][c]=O[r][c-1]
    comps=components(O)
    items=[]
    for v,cells in comps:
        rs=sorted(set(r for r,_ in cells)); cs=sorted(set(c for _,c in cells))
        if len(rs)>1:                      # vertical strip/tall
            L=cs[0]
        elif len(cs)>1:                    # horizontal bar
            g=[c for c in range(cs[0],cs[-1]+1) if O[rs[0]][c]==0]
            L=g[0] if g else cs[0]
        else:                              # single cell
            L=cells[0][1]
        items.append((v,rs[0],rs[-1],L))
    R=[row[:] for row in O]
    bycol=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for v,st,br,L in items: bycol[L].append((v,st,br))
    for L,segs in bycol.items():
        segs.sort(key=lambda x:x[1])
        prev=-1
        for v,st,br in segs:
            s=max(prev+1,0)
            for rr in range(s,br+1): R[rr][L]=v
            prev=br
    return R

import json, collections
def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    O=[row[:] for row in I]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if O[r][c]==0 and c>0 and c<W-1 and O[r][c-1]!=0 and O[r][c+1]!=0 and O[r][c-1]==O[r][c+1]:
                O[r][c]=O[r][c-1]
    comps=components(O)
    out=[row[:] for row in O]
    bycol=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for v,cells in comps:
        rs=sorted(set(r for r,_ in cells)); cs=sorted(set(c for _,c in cells))
        if len(rs)>1:                     # vertical strip: its column
            L=cs[0]
        elif len(cs)==1:                  # single cell: its column
            L=cs[0]
        else:                             # horizontal bar
            g=[c for c in range(cs[0],cs[-1]+1) if O[rs[0]][c]==0]
            L=g[0] if g else cs[0]
        bycol[L].append((v,rs[0],rs[-1]))
    for L,segs in bycol.items():
        prev=-1
        for v,st,br in sorted(segs,key=lambda x:x[1]):
            for rr in range(prev+1,br+1):
                out[rr][L]=v
            prev=max(prev,br)
    return out

Now analyze the actual transformation.

Pattern: colored horizontal bars (rows with long runs). Vertical stripes painted from bar gaps upward? Look at col 3 in demo1: input has 3s at rows 11-14; output fills rows 0-10 with 2. Color 2 comes from row 9's leftmost run [2,2,2] — but that's not column 3... hmm, but wait: the gap between the left run and right run at row 9 is at column 3. The fill of 2 fills column 3 up to where? Rows 0-10, blocked below by 3 (rows 11+). So per column, zero cells between two non-zero cells get filled with the lower one's color — EXCEPT when... in demo1 col3: above cell (row8) was zero, below at row11 =3. Fill rows0..10 with 2?? That contradicts "lower wins" unless direction: fill goes UP from the gap toward top boundary when the lower block touches bottom region? Hmm, actually simpler: each column is scanned bottom-up; a zero cell takes the color of the nearest non-zero BELOW, BUT only if it's within... in col3, cells rows0-10 all get 2, i.e., they connect to the row-9 bar via row10? No—bar is at row 9 which IS zero in col 3. Actually row9[3]=0. The "marker" is the bar's color; it extends vertically up/down through zeros until hitting another object? Col3: bar row 9 has 2 on left and 3 on right... hmm.

Alternative view: vertical stripe gets painted from the marker row upward/downward to fill the whole column except cells occupied by other objects? In demo1 col3: colors: bar 2 at row9 (left neighbor), 3-stripe at rows11-14. Output: rows0-10 = 2, rows 11-14=3. So the 2 extends up through empty cells and stops at the 3? But 2 doesn't extend down past itself. And in demo2 col3: 1-stripe rows11-14 unchanged; 4-row at row7? Wait output col3: rows0-8 = 3 then 4 rows9-13? Actually output col3: [3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,...]. Input col3 had 1 at rows11-14 and nothing else. Where does 3 come from? Row 3 has [3,3,3,0,3...] gap at col3. And 4 comes from row7 gap... row6 has 6s at cols6-8 and 10-14; row8 has 4s at 0-2,7-8. Gap in row7/8 at col3 = none contiguous. Hmm col3 output rows0-8 = 3 means 3 fills from its own bar row (row3, gap col3) upward AND downward! Row3[3]=0, neighbors 3. Output col3 rows0-8 = 3, rows 9-13 = 4?? Wait row9[3]=0 in input, output row9[3]=4. 4-bar: row8 has 4 at cols0-2 and 4 at 7-8? Actually row8 input: [4,4,4,0,4,4,4,7,7,0,...]. So 4's bar spans 0-8 with gap at col3. Then output: rows0-8 = 3 for col3... conflict: both 3 and 4 claim column 3! 

Ah-ha: overlapping claims resolved: who wins? Demo1 col3: 2-wins over nothing (no competing bar). Demo2 col3: 3 vs 4 → 3 wins. Demo3 col1: inputs: row3 has [8,0,8,8,8...] gap col1, 8s; row5 6s gap col1; row8 3s gap col1; row11 9s gap col1; single-cell markers: 7 at row2 col6-8 (vertical?), 1 at row14 col1, 1 at col9. Output col1: [8,8,8,8,3,3,3,3,3,9,9,9,1,1,1]. So order: 8(row3), 3(row8), 9(row11), 1(row14) — from top to bottom. And colors are assigned in the order of the bars sorted by their row. Each bar's gap column is filled for the segment starting just below previous bar's bottom... check: rows0-8 = 8 (from row3 bar, spanning up to row8 exclusive? no, rows 0-8 includes row 8 which is the 3-bar row). Row 8 col1 = 3. So segments: 8 covers rows 0-3? but shows 0-8. Hmm confusing because multiple bars' fill regions may merge? Bar row3: gap col1; fill upward from row3: rows0-2? plus downward to just before next bar? Next bar (3) at row8. So fill rows 0-7 = 8. Then 3 fills rows 9-10 until next bar (9) at row11: rows 9-10 = 3. Then 9: rows 12-13. Then 1: row14. Matches output exactly! Check demo2 col3: bars: 3 at row3, 4 at row8, 1 at row11. Fill: 3 covers rows0-7; 4 covers rows 9-10? but output rows 9-13 = 4?? Output col3 rows: [3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,1,...]: rows 9-13 = 4?? row9 is first row of 1's bar? No, 1's bar is row11. Wait recheck: row11 input has 1 at col3. Output row11 col3=1. So 4 fills rows 9-10?? but output shows 4 through row13! Hmm, let me re-read output row by row col3: r0:3,r1:3,r2:3,r3:3, r4:4,r5:4,r6:4,r7:4, r8:4, r9:1... wait no I read wrong earlier. Earlier diff said output col3 = [3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1]. Yes rows 4-8 = 4, rows 9+ = 1. OK matches: 4 fills rows 4-8 (between bar row 8, extending up from bar top). And 1 fills rows 9-14 (extends down from bar row 11! or up?). Bar row11: extends down through remaining rows 12-14. Or extends up? rows 9-14 all 1 including row 11. If rule "fill entire span between consecutive bars": 4 covers rows 4-8, 1 covers 9-14 (rest). Consistent with: each bar fills from its position to the edge / until next bar.

Check demo1 col3: 2-bar row9, 3-stripe rows 11-14. 2 fills rows 0-8 (up from bar? bar is at 9, fills 0-8 above and down to row 10, stopping before 3 starts). 3 keeps rows 11+. Consistent: each bar fills the gap to the next bar.

Demo3 col9: bars: 7 at row2, 6 at row5, 5 at row11, 1 at row14. Output col9: rows0-1 = 7, rows2 = 7? output col9 rows: r0:7,r1:7,r2:7?,r3:6... Let me verify: out r2 col9 = 7, r3:6,r4:6,r5:6, r6-r8:5? output says col9 out: [7,7,7,6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5,1,1,1]. Bars at rows 2,5,11,14. Segments: 7 covers 0-2, 6 covers 3-5, 5 covers 6-10, 1 covers 12-14. Perfect: each bar fills from its row to next bar row -1 (or grid bottom if last). Direction: always toward the next bar below, filling ALL zeros between. What about non-gap columns? Single-cell markers like 1 at (14,1): bar width 1 → its column fills from its row to bottom (toward next bar). And vertical strips pass through. Also what about columns with no bars at all? Unchanged.

But wait demo1 col3: 2's fill stopped at row 10, before 3's bar. And 3's bar kept original rows 11-14 (not extended further down since it's last). Also demo2 col3: 4's fill went rows 4-8 — bar at 8, fills upward to previous bar (row3) row +1. Consistent: fill spans between consecutive bars in that column.

What about overlapping claims from different columns — ignore.

Now check demo2 col 7-8: row8 has 7,7 at cols 7,8; output col7 rows6-8? output col7: r0-5:0? From out: rows show [0]*7 then [7,7] ... out col7 rows0-6=0, rows7-8=7. Fine unchanged mostly.

Also demo3 row2 has 7 at cols6-8 and 7 at cols10-14: gap col9 filled by 7 (next bar). Col 6: bars: 8 at row3, 6 at row5, 3 at row8, 5 at row11, 1 at row14? But col6 output rows: [0,0,8,8,3,3,5,5,5,9,9,9,1,1,1]? Expected col6 output: r2:r2=7 originally stays? Output col6: [0,0,8,8,3,3,5,5,5,9,9,9,1,1,1]. 1 appears at col6 though no 1 bar in col6. Hmm — that's interesting: 1-bar is a single cell at (14,1) and (14,9). Column 6 gets 1 from... the bottom? Wait maybe rule: fill also extends DOWNWARD from bar when bar is last, and single-cell markers get treated as bars filling to the bottom. For col1: 1 at row14 fills rows 12-14 (down to bottom). For col6, 9-bar at row11 fills 9,10,11 and 1 continues 12-14 (down to bottom). So general rule: fill downward from bar until next bar or grid bottom; fill upward until previous bar or grid top. So full-column segmentation by bars: each bar's color occupies the interval [prev_bottom+1, curr_top-1] union its own row... simpler: in each column, mark rows containing a bar (any length ≥1 run?) ; sort unique rows; fill each interval.

Wait but demo1 col3: 2 at row9 fills 0-10; 3 at rows11-14 keeps 11-14. But 3 is a multi-row stripe — treat each row separately. Fine.

Now handle multi-run rows: multiple gaps per row — e.g., demo2 row3: gaps at col3 and cols 8? [3,3,3,0,3,3,3,0,...]: gaps col3 only up to col7? cols 3 and 7? row3=[3,3,3,0,3,3,3,0,...] gap at 3 and 7. Both filled with 3 (output col3 and col7 both got 3? col7 output rows 3-8 = 7... let me check: out row8 col7=7, out row9 col7=0? From earlier printout: out row8=[4,4,4,4,4,4,4,7,7,7,7,7,7,7,7], so col7=7 at row8 only. Hmm col7 got 7 only. So gap at col3 gets 3, gap at col7 gets nothing?! Because 3's bar fill: interval between row3 and row8 → only col3 (the gap adjacent between runs)? Col7 gap at row3 falls outside any fill? Its interval would be rows 4-8 but filled with what? Nothing → remains 0 except row8's 7 at col7,8 which is the 7 bar at row8. Actually output col7: only row 8. So gap at col3 filled by 3 (interval rows 0-7? no rows 4-8 are 4...). Ugh, mixed.

New idea: gaps get filled by the color of the LEFT neighbor? Gap col3 neighbors: 3(left), 3(right) → 3. Gap col7 neighbors: 3(left), 0(right)? row3 col7=0, col8=0? Row3: [3,3,3,0,3,3,3,0,0,...] col7=0,col8=0. Hmm both zero. Filled by 3 anyway (left).

Alternative: fill gaps by nearest bar on... Let me think of it as: each maximal horizontal run is an object; each object fills upward and downward through empty cells in its column range? Run [3,3,3] cols0-2 row3: fills up/down in cols0-2 — no effect. Gap fill: maybe each gap column belongs to the run whose gap it is, and fill extends the column up and down to boundaries defined by other objects' rows in that column. Col3: 3 fills rows 0-7 and 9-10?? No—output col3 rows 0-7 = 3? Earlier: [3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,...] → rows0-3 = 3, rows4-8=4, rows9-13=1, row14=1. But wait rows 4-8 = 4? That contradicts 3's fill. Unless: 3's fill is only rows 0-3?? and 4 fills 4-8, 1 fills 9-14. Then 3 fills only its own bar rows (row3) plus... rows 0-2? Those came from? Hmm — maybe fill direction: only downward? No: demo1 col3 2 fills rows 0-10 (both up and down).

Let me reconsider demo2 col3 fully:
in col3: rows0-10=0, rows11-14=1. out: 0-8=3, 9-13=4, 14=1?? Wait output col3 rows: [3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1] per earlier diff listing (rows 9-14=1). So 3 fills 0-8, 4 fills 9-13, 1 fills 14. No! 1's bar at row 11 is inside segment 9-13 which belongs to 4. Contradiction.

Unless bars don't own by containment but assign intervals: sorted bar rows 3,8,11 → intervals [0,7],[8,10],[11,14]?? That gives 3:[0,7], 4:[8,10], 1:[11,14]. But observed 3:[0,8] and 4:[9,13]. Collision region rows 0-7 contested by 3(upshoot) and 4(downshoot). Result: 3 wins rows 0-8?? weird.

Hmm, alternatively: shoots go down ONLY? 3 fills 0-8? no.

Try: each bar fills the gap between itself and the NEAREST BAR below (exclusive), AND between itself and nearest bar above (exclusive). 3's nearest below = 8: fill 0-7? observed 0-8. Hmm still off.
